record.paper_title: A survey of equivariant map algebras with open problems
record.original_question: When a is an associative algebra and M = M(X,a)^Γ, go beyond the classification of irreducible finite-dimensional M-modules and describe all indecomposable finite-dimensional modules, together with the block decomposition of the corresponding module category.

evidence.quote: 4.2.3. Indecomposable modules. The classification of the irreducible objects in the category of finite-dimensional modules of M for an associative a in Theorem 2.1 is only a first step towards a complete understanding of the category. Ideally, one would like to describe all of the indecomposable finite-dimensional modules and understand the block decomposition of this category.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let X be an affine scheme of finite type over an algebraically closed field k of characteristic zero, and let a be a finite-dimensional associative k-algebra. Let Γ be a finite group acting on X (by automorphisms of the coordinate ring A = k[X]) and on a (by k-algebra automorphisms). Form the equivariant map algebra
   M = M(X, a)^Γ := (A ⊗_k a)^Γ,
the fixed-point subalgebra of A ⊗ a under the diagonal Γ-action. Consider the category Mod_fd(M) of finite-dimensional left M-modules.

It is known that every irreducible object in Mod_fd(M) is isomorphic to a tensor product of evaluation representations (twisted appropriately by Γ). The problem is to go beyond this:

(a) Classify, up to isomorphism, all indecomposable objects of Mod_fd(M).
(b) Describe explicitly the block decomposition of the category Mod_fd(M), i.e., determine the equivalence classes under the relation generated by "there exists a nonzero extension between two irreducibles," and describe each block as a category.
artifact.status_search_result: The block decomposition of the category of finite-dimensional representations of equivariant map (Lie) algebras has been described in terms of spectral characters by Neher–Savage (Transformation Groups, 2015) for X affine of finite type and g reductive, and analogous results have been obtained for equivariant map superalgebras. However, a complete classification of all indecomposable finite-dimensional modules over equivariant map algebras (in the associative-algebra setting M(X,a)^Γ) remains open in general; only partial results (e.g. local Weyl modules as indecomposables, extensions between irreducibles) are known.

status_evidence.title: Extensions and block decompositions for finite-dimensional representations of equivariant map algebras
status_evidence.snippet: Describes extensions between irreducible finite-dimensional representations of an equivariant map algebra and gives the block decomposition in terms of spectral characters.
status_evidence.claim: Block decomposition is known for equivariant map (Lie) algebras with X affine of finite type and g reductive.

status_evidence.title: Irreducible modules for equivariant map superalgebras and their extensions
status_evidence.snippet: Extends classification and extension results to equivariant map superalgebras.
status_evidence.claim: Partial results on extensions and blocks exist in related (super) settings.

status_evidence.title: A survey of equivariant map algebras with open problems
status_evidence.snippet: Listed as an open problem: describe all indecomposable finite-dimensional modules and the block decomposition.
status_evidence.claim: Full classification of indecomposable finite-dimensional modules is posed as open.
